narrative.overview:
Every statutory due date runs on a timetable, so the workstation reads like one. The system borrows from the Indian Railways printed timetable, Trains at a Glance and the station boards: a solid navy shell, an off-white page, dense condensed figures in strict columns, dates printed once per group like departure times, and status read off a signal. The world lends type, palette, density and one signature move. Layout, navigation and controls stay those of a standard professional web app (rail, command bar, tabs, tables, inspector), so an accountant knows where everything is before they notice the world.

Density is the point. Rows are 28px, body text is 13px, and the working sheet is one white surface divided by hairlines rather than a floor of cards. Hierarchy comes from figure size and weight on that sheet, never from shadows or tinted boxes. Saturated colour exists only to carry state: the four signal aspects. Charts never lead; where a bar appears it carries counts that are also printed beside it.

The physical scene decided the light theme: partners and article assistants at office desktops, under daylight and tube lights, eight to ten hours a day, with portal PDFs and WhatsApp open alongside.
keyCharacteristics: Navy rail and command bar; off-white ground; white working sheet divided by 1px hairlines.
Archivo at two widths: normal for interface text, condensed for figures, dates and column heads.
The four-aspect signal head on every list, always paired with a "late by" or "due in" figure.
Timetable rhythm in tables: date printed once per group, a stronger rule every fifth row, a double rule between groups.
URL-addressable views: every tab, filter and selection is a link, so any view can be saved or shared.

rules.name: The Signal-Only Rule
rules.body: Red, yellow and green appear only as state. Never as decoration, category colour, brand accent or chart series.

rules.name: The Never-Alone Rule
rules.body: A signal is always accompanied by text that says the same thing: a "late by" figure, a status word, or an accessible label. Colour is never the only cue.

rules.name: The One-Field Shell Rule
rules.body: The rail and the command bar are one flat navy field. No gradients, no glass, no second shell colour.

rules.name: The Two-Width Rule
rules.body: One family. Interface text at normal width; figures, dates and column heads condensed. No second typeface.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Any number that can stack in a column is tabular and lining: amounts, counts, dates, hours.

rules.name: The Indian Figures Rule
rules.body: Money uses en-IN grouping (₹12,34,567); summaries use lakh and crore (₹3.84 L, ₹1.26 Cr); dates are DD/MM/YYYY and times IST.

rules.name: The Timetable Rhythm Rule
rules.body: In grouped tables the group key (usually the due date) prints once, on the first row. Every fifth row carries the strong rule; groups are separated by a double rule.

rules.name: The Addressable View Rule
rules.body: Tabs, filters, view toggles and the selected row live in the URL. A saved view is a link.

rules.name: The Float-Only Shadow Rule
rules.body: If it does not float over other content, it has no shadow. Panels, tables and the inspector column are flat.

dos: Do pair every signal with a figure or word ("17d late", "in 3d", "Awaiting data").
Do set money with en-IN grouping, summaries in lakh and crore, dates as DD/MM/YYYY, times in IST, and FY as April to March.
Do put identifiers (PAN, GSTIN, ARN) in the identifier style, with a copy affordance where they are pasted into portals.
Do divide regions with 1px hairlines on one white sheet; use the strong rule for every fifth row and the double rule between groups.
Do keep filters, tabs and selection in the URL so views are shareable and keyboard navigation works.
Do drop secondary columns at narrower widths instead of letting the last column clip.
donts: Don't use red, yellow or green for anything but state.
Don't float panels as cards or give flat surfaces shadows; only overlays, menus and the mobile sheet carry shadows.
Don't lead a screen with a row of KPI tiles or a chart; lead with the list that needs action.
Don't add a second typeface or a monospace; condense Archivo for figures instead.
Don't put a small label or eyebrow above a heading, or a coloured stripe down the side of a row or panel.
Don't use Unicode glyphs or emoji as icons; icons are drawn (Lucide, 1.75 to 2 stroke).
